title: Drug development & trials
examples: What is the difference between preclinical and clinical testing?
Why is it important that the study is double-blind?
How does a placebo work in drug trials?

explain.say: First we look at preclinical testing for new drugs.
Next we move to clinical trials in humans.
A double-blind study keeps people and staff guessing.
A placebo is an inactive substance used for comparison.
In real life, testing a new headache medicine uses these steps.
A common mistake is forgetting to use a placebo.

items: Results might be due to expectation

faq.q: What is the main purpose of preclinical testing?
faq.a: Preclinical testing happens before human trials begin. It tests the drug's safety and basic effects on cells and animals.
asks: Do they test drugs on people first?
What happens before human trials start?

faq.q: Why is the double-blind method so important in trials?
faq.a: It stops expectations from changing the results. Neither the patient nor the doctor knows who gets the real medicine.
asks: What does double-blind mean for results?
Why can't doctors know who gets what?

faq.q: Can you explain what a placebo is exactly?
faq.a: A placebo is an inactive substance given to some participants. It helps researchers measure the drug's true effect against the mind's expectation.
asks: What is the purpose of the sugar pill?

faq.q: Are the phases of clinical trials always in this order?
faq.a: Yes, the phases generally move from small safety groups to large effectiveness groups. This builds safety before testing effectiveness.
asks: Do I go from Phase 1 to Phase 3?
What is the order of human testing?

faq.q: How long does the whole drug development process take?
faq.a: It takes many years, involving multiple stages of testing. Each stage must show safety before moving to the next one.
asks: How many years does it take to make a drug?

facts: Preclinical testing involves laboratory and animal studies.
Clinical trials are divided into phases to test safety and effectiveness.
A double-blind study ensures no one knows who gets the active drug.
A placebo is an inert substance used as a control group.

quiz.say: Testing a drug on cells and animals happens during which stage?
quiz.why: This stage happens before any human testing begins.

wrong.0: Phase 1 is the first time testing on human volunteers.
wrong.1: Double-blind describes the method, not the stage.
wrong.2: Placebo is the substance used for comparison, not the stage.

quiz.say: If a study is double-blind, what does that mean for the participants?
quiz.show: No one knows who gets what

options.show: They do not know if they receive the real drug or placebo.
options.say: They do not know if they receive the real drug or placebo.

options.show: They know the study is happening
options.say: They know the study is happening

quiz.why: This prevents their expectations from affecting the measured results.

wrong.0: The doctors must also be kept unaware to avoid bias.
wrong.1: They must receive one of the two tested substances.
wrong.3: Knowing the study is happening can cause anxiety.

quiz.say: What is the purpose of giving a placebo in a trial?

options.show: Because the drug is too strong for people
options.say: Because the drug is too strong for people

options.show: To make the trial look more complicated
options.say: To make the trial look more complicated

options.show: To measure the drug's effect beyond expectation.
options.say: To measure the drug's effect beyond expectation.

options.show: To trick the participants into thinking it works
options.say: To trick the participants into thinking it works

quiz.why: It provides a baseline measurement against the drug's actual effect.

wrong.0: The placebo is used regardless of the drug's strength.
wrong.1: It is a necessary scientific control, not a complication.
wrong.3: While it mimics this, its scientific purpose is measurement.
